record.context_brief: forms and evolution of Galactic antimatter domains
record.original_question: In nonhomogeneous baryosynthesis models where the sign of baryon excess can change and create antimatter domains surrounded by matter, what forms of macroscopic antimatter objects can exist in the Galaxy, and how do antibaryon domains evolve in a baryon-asymmetric Universe under the constraints that surviving Galactic antimatter domains have masses roughly between 10^3 and 10^5 solar masses?

evidence.quote: If baryosynthesis is inhomogeneous, in the extreme case the sign of the baryon excess can change, giving rise to antimatter domains, produced in the same process, in which the baryon asymmetry is created [39, 28, 40, 41, 42, 43]. Such antimatter domains are surrounded by matter. They should be sufficiently large to survive to the present time and to give rise to antimatter objects in the Galaxy.
These limits give the interval of mass M of antimatter in our Galaxy 10^3M⊙ ≤ M ≤ 10^5M⊙, which is typical for globular clusters.

Therefore, studies of possible forms of macroscopic antimatter objects in our Galaxy are challenging, involving evolution of antibaryon domains in baryon asymmetrical universe [46, 47] in the context of models of non-homogeneous baryosynthesis.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a class of cosmological baryogenesis scenarios in which the generation of the baryon asymmetry is spatially nonhomogeneous, so that the sign of the local baryon excess can vary across the Universe. In such a scenario, regions of net antibaryon excess (antimatter domains) are produced by the same dynamical process that produces the dominant baryon excess, and these antimatter domains are embedded within a matter-dominated background. After cosmological evolution (including diffusion, annihilation at domain boundaries, and gravitational collapse), only sufficiently large antimatter domains can survive until the present epoch and form macroscopic antimatter objects in a galaxy comparable to the Milky Way. Assume the surviving antimatter mass M contained in any single Galactic antimatter object is constrained to lie in the interval

   10^3 M_⊙  ≤  M  ≤  10^5 M_⊙,

where M_⊙ denotes one solar mass.

Problem. Within this framework, determine:
(a) the complete classification of possible forms of macroscopic antimatter objects (e.g. anti-stars, anti-stellar clusters, compact anti-clouds, anti-black-holes formed from collapse of anti-domains, etc.) that can exist in such a galaxy consistent with the above mass interval; and
(b) the quantitative dynamical evolution of an antibaryon domain of given initial size, shape, and antibaryon-to-photon ratio embedded in a baryon-asymmetric cosmological background, from the epoch of baryogenesis through recombination, structure formation, and Galactic evolution, including the conditions on the initial domain parameters under which the surviving mass falls into the prescribed window 10^3–10^5 M_⊙.
artifact.status_search_result: The classification and detailed evolution of antimatter domains in inhomogeneous baryogenesis remains an active research topic without a complete resolution. Recent reviews and works by Khlopov and collaborators continue to discuss the problem as an open challenge, listing candidate forms (anti-stellar globular-cluster-like objects, anti-clouds, anti-nuclei) without a definitive classification or fully worked-out evolutionary theory.

status_evidence.title: Open questions of BSM Cosmology (review)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies of possible forms of macroscopic antimatter objects in our Galaxy are challenging, involving evolution of antibaryon domains in baryon asymmetrical universe.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of classifying surviving antimatter objects and modeling antibaryon domain evolution is explicitly described as a current open challenge.

status_evidence.title: Fundamental cosmology from BSM physics (Khlopov)
status_evidence.snippet: Antimatter domains in baryon asymmetrical Universe and their evolution into anti-matter objects in the Galaxy remain a subject of ongoing investigation.
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature still treats the dynamical evolution and surviving forms of Galactic antimatter domains as unresolved.
